newhire_jen: Hey team — quick question. I'm on my first week and trying to call the hosted API from my laptop, but I'm getting a `429 rate_limit_exceeded` response. I thought sandbox keys were unlimited? :confused:

maya_devex: Welcome, Jen! :tada: Sandbox keys are not unlimited — they're meant for dev/testing so they have fairly low quotas and lower QPS. Which key are you using (hosted vs sandbox)?

newhire_jen: I grabbed the key from the email with the subject 'Welcome to Redwood' — the env var they told me to set is `REDWOOD_API_KEY`. Not sure if that's the hosted key or sandbox. The console UI is a bit confusing to me.

sam_infra: If it came from the onboarding email it's usually a Sandbox key. Hosted keys require billing to be set up. In Console go to Console > API keys and you'll see two sections: "Sandbox keys" and "Hosted/API keys". Sandbox shows as "dev" and has a little sandbox badge.

newhire_jen: Ah OK found it. I see a key in Sandbox with label "jen-sandbox-1". Is there a way to check what my current quota/usage is so I know why I'm hitting 429s?

maya_devex: Yes — Console > Usage (or Billing > API usage) shows token usage and rate limit windows per key. Also responses include headers you can inspect. Try this to see headers: ```curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/outputs``` Look for `x-ratelimit-limit` / `x-ratelimit-remaining` or similar.

newhire_jen: Ran that and saw `x-ratelimit-remaining: 0` and `x-ratelimit-reset: 30`. So that explains it. Is there a simple way to get a slightly higher sandbox quota for doing a demo?

maya_devex: We can temporary bump sandbox limits for onboarding demos. Ping `#devex` or reply here with your team and demo time and we can request an increase. For longer-term higher QPS you need hosted keys and a billing profile.

jordan_oncall: FYI sandbox QPS defaults to 5 requests/sec and daily token quota ~100k for new hires (varies by cohort). If you need burst for a 10–15 minute demo we can open a short-lived increase.

newhire_jen: That'd be great — I have a lightning demo tomorrow at 2pm PT showing streaming. I'll need ~20rps for ~5 minutes.

sam_infra: Noted. @maya_devex can you submit an ad-hoc increase? We usually set a 10-min burst limit in the backend. Also, for streaming tests use the `stream=true` param and prefer 1 connection with more tokens rather than many small requests — that helps stay under QPS.

maya_devex: On it. @newhire_jen please DM me your request details and I'll route it. Meanwhile, for local dev you can lower concurrency or add exponential backoff to avoid repeated 429s. Example snippet: ```python
# naive backoff
import time
for attempt in range(5):
  resp = call_api()
  if resp.status_code == 200:
    break
  if resp.status_code == 429:
    wait = 2 ** attempt
    time.sleep(wait)
```

newhire_jen: Thanks all — helps a lot. One last thing: are there separate per-key rate limits vs per-account? I want to know if my sandbox traffic will affect others on my org account.

sam_infra: Good Q. Sandbox keys are per-user and separate; they don't consume org hosted capacity. Hosted keys are billed and have account-level quotas depending on plan.

maya_devex: Also check that you aren't accidentally sharing the sandbox key in CI or with teammates — if it's used elsewhere it can exhaust your quota quickly.

newhire_jen: Got it. I'll DM @maya_devex the demo details. Appreciate the quick help! :heart:

devex-bot: Reminder: For sandbox increase requests, include (1) key id, (2) start/end time (UTC), (3) expected RPS, (4) reason. Example: `jen-sandbox-1, 2026-03-24T21:00Z -> 2026-03-24T21:15Z, 20rps, demo streaming feature.`

jordan_oncall: If you still see weird 429s after increase, paste the full `x-request-id` header and we'll trace it.
